title: How Grand Theft Auto changed gaming, and why GTA VI has so much to live up to
content_html:
Lucia and Jason, the protagonists of Grand Theft Auto VI. The latest instalment in Rockstar Games’ nearly 30-year-old franchise places greater emphasis on relationships, realism and the consequences of players’ actions. (Photo: Rockstar Games)

After 13 years of waiting for a game that managed to spawn a generation of memes about milestones that were achieved before its release, Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI was launched worldwide on Thursday (November 19).

The game is the latest instalment of a nearly 30-year-old franchise that began as a crime-themed video game and evolved into a sprawling satire of American society. Created in Scotland, the franchise has since become one of the most recognisable names in gaming.

On Friday, Rockstar Games said GTA VI had generated $3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day, setting what it described as a record for an entertainment launch across any medium. The publisher said 32.5 million copies had been sold ahead of the release.

Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads.

The latest release centres on two new characters, Jason and Lucia, a couple whose lives revolve around petty crime in a fictionalised version of Florida. But early reviews suggest that GTA VI is also departing from some of the conventions that made its predecessors famous, placing greater emphasis on relationships and making players confront the consequences of their actions.

— zacianzz (@suaspontes) November 21, 2026

The changes raise an interesting question about a franchise long associated with violence, controversy and the freedom to cause chaos: how did GTA become such a defining part of video game culture, and what does its latest evolution mean for the legacy it has built?

From cops and robbers to a virtual world

Grand Theft Auto debuted in 1997 as a straightforward game that granted players the freedom to steal cars, commit crimes and complete missions. Players viewed the action from overhead, navigating fictional American cities while completing missions.

“Rockstar Games’ ambition with Grand Theft Auto was to essentially prove that the interactive medium can be just as compelling and gripping as film and television,” Sujay Nellore, a long-time GTA fan who has played the series since its debut in 1997, told The Indian Express. “It started small, but they have iterated and innovated with every single mainline entry into the franchise.”

The turning point came with GTA III, released in 2001. Set in Liberty City, a fictionalised version of New York City, the game cemented the franchise’s visual identity. It introduced the distinctive logo typography borrowed from the TV show The Price Is Right, along with the illustrated, checkerboard-style cover art that subsequent instalments retained.

Story continues below this ad

The game moved the action into a fully three-dimensional environment. Instead of viewing the city from overhead, players could follow their character at street level, exploring the city and completing missions in a more immersive world. It introduced more cinematic storytelling, with voice acting by Hollywood actors Michael Madsen, Kyle MacLachlan and Frank Vincent.

Game designer turned academic Bob de Schutter told The Indian Express that GTA III put the genre of open-world games into the spotlight. “Its structure of story missions spread across a massive city is still the template for open-world games. It also made strides in storytelling, bringing many movie tropes into games,” he added.

The game’s influence extended beyond Rockstar. Former PlayStation Studios chief Shuhei Yoshida told The Game Business podcast that the success of GTA III, Vice City and San Andreas influenced the direction of several Sony-owned studios. Naughty Dog, Insomniac Games and Sucker Punch, which had previously developed games featuring cartoonish characters, subsequently moved towards more mature, realistic action-adventure titles, including Uncharted, Resistance: Fall of Man and Infamous.

Also Read | GTA 6, Modi and the BJP’s bid to crack the Gen Z audience

For Nellore, the franchise’s evolution went beyond improvements in graphics and gameplay. “At its core, GTA retains this to this day, but now we have richly detailed worlds within which your actions as a player make sense. You now have player characters that have strong motivations, things they want to do, lines they won’t cross,” he said.

Story continues below this ad

GTA: Vice City, released in 2002, was a cinematic gangster fantasy set in a fictionalised Miami, drawing heavily on Scarface and Miami Vice. GTA: San Andreas, released in 2004, featured a larger world comprising fictionalised versions of Los Angeles, San Francisco and Las Vegas, while exploring gang culture and social divisions.

GTA’s America: satire and the American Dream

As the worlds grew more elaborate, so did the stories Rockstar sought to tell. Nellore points to GTA IV (2008), whose protagonist, Niko Bellic, is a veteran of the Yugoslav wars struggling with his past and his pursuit of a better life in America.

The game took a decidedly political tone, trading the bright, neon-lit settings of earlier instalments for a greyer, more sombre world that highlighted the debt and hardships faced by an immigrant in the US. Released in April 2008, as the US was entering a recession, it also gave its protagonist a more complex personal history. GTA IV was arguably Rockstar’s most ambitious release yet.

“Rockstar saw the blending of narrative and gameplay and made GTA IV, with leading man Niko Bellic, who was their best-written character to date,” Nellore said.

Story continues below this ad

The American Dream has remained a recurring theme across the franchise. John Wills, professor of American Studies at the University of Kent, told The Indian Express that GTA represented a case of the “tourist gaze”, calling it an outsider exploration of what America symbolises. “Rockstar’s work is like a 21st-century version of Alexis de Tocqueville, a French philosopher, visiting America in the 1830s and writing about it: an outsider’s lens on the American experiment,” he said.

In GTA V (2013), Rockstar explored the contradictions of the American Dream through three protagonists, including Michael, a wealthy but disillusioned former criminal, and Franklin, a young Black man seeking to escape poverty. The game also satirised American consumerism, corporate culture and political institutions through its fictional advertisements, radio programmes and missions.

Wills points to billboards advertising ammunition or promising poor service on domestic flights, Michael’s counselling sessions in which he expresses disillusionment with the American Dream, and missions that involve attacking American technology businesses. The satire, he argues, is embedded in practically every aspect of the game world.

Unlike television satire, players actively participate in Rockstar’s fictional society. “We are active in the satirical playground – we experience it and even shape it. We are part of Rockstar’s message,” Wills told The Indian Express.

Story continues below this ad

How GTA has remained relevant for 13 years

Despite the 13-year gap between GTA V and GTA VI, the franchise never really disappeared. A major reason was GTA Online, the multiplayer component of GTA V, which allowed players to explore Los Santos together, undertake missions and stage elaborate heists.

For Nellore, this was key to the game’s longevity. “What really blew up was GTA Online, which brought the central feature of GTA V – the Michael Mann movie-style heists – into a cooperative multiplayer setting where you could team up with your friends and go on heists together,” he said.

Rockstar continued to introduce new missions, activities and other content over the years. Meanwhile, players created their own characters and stories through role-playing communities, attracting audiences on YouTube and Twitch. In 2023, Rockstar acquired Cfx.re, the team behind FiveM, which enabled customised GTA V multiplayer servers.

Nellore, who has played GTA since the late 1990s, said the franchise’s audience had also changed. While older players such as himself preferred its single-player stories, newer audiences increasingly sought multiplayer experiences.

Story continues below this ad

The commercial success of GTA V and GTA Online also gave Rockstar the financial freedom to invest enormous resources in its next instalment. As Nellore put it, “For a studio that is as detail-oriented, as dedicated to ensuring a coherent open world, as strict as ensuring their writing is top-notch, that means they can take their time with the product.”

How GTA VI is challenging the franchise’s conventions

Over the years, the franchise has attracted sustained criticism for its violence and portrayal of women, particularly sex workers. Its games allowed players to attack police officers and innocent bystanders, while critics accused Rockstar of glamourising criminal behaviour.

“The GTA franchise is primarily a male fantasy. Women are in the games to be seen and interacted with through a male gaze. And Rockstar has often courted controversy by deliberately including strip clubs and objectifying women,” Wills said.

The satire itself was not without contradictions. As Wills has argued in his research, the games frequently reward players for pursuing wealth and violence, even while their stories criticise the excesses of American society.

Story continues below this ad

The controversies also contributed to the franchise’s notoriety. “It’s the video game equivalent of slapping a parental advisory sticker on a rap album: all those stickers did was make these albums more sought after,” Nellore said.

Early reviews, however, suggest that GTA VI is challenging some of the conventions the franchise has long been known for.

— POPTime (@poptime) November 19, 2026

The game introduces a more responsive and realistic world. Players can still steal cars, commit crimes and cause chaos, but evading the police has become more difficult, with surveillance systems and more sophisticated police responses. Everyday activities have also become part of the experience, from maintaining vehicles and decorating homes to scuba diving and birdwatching, Reuters reported on Saturday.

For Nellore, the change reflects how the franchise has matured alongside its audience. “GTA as a series has grown up with the people who played it. What used to be the thoughtless act of committing a crime in, say, GTA 3 has now been replaced by the game’s systems encouraging you to think about your actions before you commit the crime,” he said.

He sees the increased friction in gameplay as the franchise’s biggest innovation, making players more conscious of the decisions they take as Jason and Lucia.

Story continues below this ad

The changes also extend to how players interact with the protagonists. Players can choose to spend time with Lucia and Jason as a couple, holding hands, going on dates or looking after each other. Reviews suggest that neglecting the relationship can affect how the characters interact and influence the story itself.

Rockstar’s developers have also described the relationship as central to the game’s storytelling. In an interview with Game Informer, the studio explained how allowing Jason and Lucia to interact outside scripted missions gave players greater influence over their relationship.

Wills, who had not yet played the game at the time of this conversation, viewed the introduction of a female protagonist as having “threatened one of the foundations of GTA as a ‘man’s world’.”

Also in Explained | Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond. How is 007 cast?

“Depending on how the game/story plays out, this could be a very welcome shift in GTA towards inclusivity and a breakthrough title for the company. But more likely, there will be overtones of welcome progress and some interesting character development, but players will still be able to find at least some of the old Rockstar sexualised content along the way.”

There is also a tension between greater realism and the freedom that has long defined GTA. De Schutter pointed out that allowing players to decide when to advance the story makes it difficult for developers to build narrative tension in the way a film editor can.

Wills raised a similar concern about GTA VI. He compared its increasing emphasis on everyday activities with Rockstar’s Red Dead Redemption 2, which introduced elements such as personal hygiene and maintaining a camp into its depiction of frontier life.

“However, the more real a game gets, maybe the sense of the game as fun and escape decreases. That is a danger,” he said.

title: ‘We got this before GTA 6’: Why the BJP and Congress are invoking a viral meme in their political battle
content_html:
GTA 6's launch sparked a political exchange in India, with BJP highlighting the country's progress since 2013 and Congress questioning Modi's gaming imagery. (X/Narendra Modi, Rockstar Games)
AI Narration
Listen
00:00

The launch of Grand Theft Auto VI has given India’s political parties a new reference point in their social media messaging, with the BJP and Congress drawing on the video game’s popularity to trade political barbs.

The exchange centres on a popular internet joke about the 13-year gap between GTA V, released in 2013, and its successor, which launched worldwide on Thursday (November 19).

The BJP, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, used the comparison to highlight what it describes as India’s progress over this period. The Congress has questioned the ruling party’s decision to associate itself with a game built around criminal activity and violence.

India is playing a whole new game! https://t.co/CMkMbK6vII

— Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) November 19, 2026

First, what is GTA?

Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads.

First released in 1997, Grand Theft Auto is an open-world video game franchise in which players explore fictional American cities, undertake missions and engage in activities ranging from driving and exploration to theft and violent crime.

Developed by Rockstar Games, the series has become known for its sprawling virtual worlds, satirical portrayal of American society and the freedom it gives players to interact with their surroundings. Its best-known instalments include GTA III, Vice City, San Andreas, GTA IV and GTA V.

Players can move freely through these virtual worlds, travelling on foot or by vehicle, and undertake missions involving everything from petty theft to organised crime. The games also recreate aspects of everyday life, including phone calls and messages, while using fictional characters and businesses to satirise American society.

GTA VI follows Jason and Lucia, a couple involved in criminal activity in a fictionalised version of Florida. Like its predecessors, the game features violence and criminal missions alongside an expansive world that players can explore.

And what is the meme?

Story continues below this ad

The political exchange draws on a meme that became popular during the long wait for GTA VI: “We got [something] before GTA VI.” Internet users inserted major political events, technological developments and other milestones into the phrase to joke about how much had changed since the previous instalment.

The 13-year gap made the joke particularly adaptable to political messaging. For the BJP, it offered a way to present its account of changes in India since 2013 using a reference familiar to younger audiences. For the Congress, the game’s criminal themes provided an opportunity to ridicule the Prime Minister’s choice of imagery.

The franchise’s popularity added to the attention surrounding the exchange. Rockstar Games, the game’s publisher, said GTA VI generated $3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day, describing it as the biggest entertainment launch in history.

How has the BJP used GTA VI?

As anticipation surrounding the game’s release grew, the Prime Minister’s X and Instagram accounts published a series of slides borrowing the franchise’s distinctive typography and imagery.

Story continues below this ad

“Between GTA V and VI, here’s how India upgraded”, the post stated, followed by images of ‘Level Up’ across various sectors from the economy and poverty alleviation to ramping up its solar power generation capacity and start-up ecosystem.

Also Read | GTA 6, Modi and the BJP’s bid to crack the Gen Z audience

The campaign used the period between the two releases to showcase the government’s claims about India’s economic growth, infrastructure development and other achievements.

According to BJP sources, the party’s social media workers had identified the trend before the game’s launch. However, the decision to capitalise on it was made following Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi’s recent interaction with students at US universities.

On Saturday (November 21), Minister of Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari’s social media account used similar imagery to highlight highway construction and reductions in travel time across the country.

Story continues below this ad

Several BJP state units and accounts associated with senior leaders, including Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, also amplified the trend.

Why has the Congress objected?

The Congress attacked the Prime Minister’s choice of imagery, pointing to the game’s central themes of crime and violence.

Congress communications in-charge Jairam Ramesh criticised the Prime Minister’s post, referring to GTA VI’s protagonists, Jason and Lucia, who are involved in criminal activity. He said in a post, “The PM in a desperate bid to reach out to the youth has resorted to GTA V and GTA VI imagery on social media. Recall that this video game follows a criminal duo. How very appropriate.”

The BJP responded by accusing the Congress of focusing on the video game’s storyline rather than engaging with the figures presented in Modi’s post.

Story continues below this ad

BJP social media co-convenor Priti Gandhi said the post was “about exposing Congress-era failures & showcasing India’s progress” since 2014. “You were unable to counter a single figure, so you chose to moralise about video-game characters…” she alleged.

The Congress also circulated a minute-long video highlighting the game’s violent themes, captioned “From Vote Chori To GTA: Modi’s Perfect Match”.

As anticipation surrounding the game’s release grew, the Prime Minister’s X and Instagram accounts published a series of slides borrowing the franchise’s distinctive typography and imagery.

“Between GTA V and VI, here’s how India upgraded”, the post stated, followed by images of ‘Level Up’ across various sectors from the economy and poverty alleviation to ramping up its solar power generation capacity and start-up ecosystem.

The campaign used the period between the two releases to showcase the government’s claims about India’s economic growth, infrastructure development and other achievements.

Nitin Gadkari
’s social media account used similar imagery to highlight highway construction and reductions in travel time across the country.

Several BJP state units and accounts associated with senior leaders, including Assam Chief Minister
Himanta Biswa Sarma
, also amplified the trend.

The Congress attacked the Prime Minister’s choice of imagery, pointing to the game’s central themes of crime and violence.
Congress communications in-charge Jairam Ramesh criticised the Prime Minister’s post, referring to GTA VI’s protagonists, Jason and Lucia, who are involved in criminal activity. title: How 2 major summits this week point to balance & bargain strategy in big-power diplomacy
content_html:
The meeting in China this week would be the first of its kind, with Presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin. (Wikimedia Commons)
AI Narration
Listen
00:00

Next week’s two summits are unlikely to set the world on fire. On Tuesday (November 17), the Quad leaders of Australia, India, Japan and the United States meet in Manila. On Thursday (November 19), Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping meet in Shenzhen. Taken together, they illuminate the rapidly changing nature of great-power politics: every major power is balancing and bargaining at the same time — simultaneously building coalitions, hedging against volatile partners and negotiating with adversaries.

This is not a world for the faint-hearted or those seeking ideological clarity. It rewards leaders who can navigate international contradictions and manage them to strengthen national capabilities.

Tuesday’s meeting in Manila of the leaders of Australia, India, Japan and the United States promises to resurrect a forum widely presumed dead. Thursday’s meeting in Shenzhen between Trump, Putin and Xi could give birth to a new format for consultations among the world’s three leading powers.

Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads.

The Quad’s agenda

The sequence is accidental but significant. Trump will meet America’s Asian partners before engaging the Chinese and Russian leaders. His preference might have been to focus on the latter, but the American establishment sees value in reassuring its allies. It also recognises that the Quad could strengthen Trump’s bargaining position with Xi and Putin.

Until recently, many had written off the Quad. The obituaries were premature. Ministerial consultations and practical cooperation continued despite the absence of summit-level engagement. Manila has an interesting place in the Quad’s history. The forum first met there in 2007. After becoming moribund, it was revived in Manila in 2017. Nearly a decade later, Manila is once again the setting for its renewal.

People gather near an installation promoting the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) China 2026 summit, in Shenzhen, China, Nov. 11. Leaders of the US, China and Russia will meet on its sidelines. (AP Photo/Ng Han Guan)

The proposed agenda is practical: critical minerals, resilient supply chains, energy security and the protection of commercial shipping. Maritime security, emerging technologies and strategic infrastructure remain important areas of cooperation.

Why G-3 is not quite a new Yalta

If Manila is renewing an established forum, Shenzhen is about launching a new one. The prospect of the American, Russian and Chinese presidents sitting together has revived speculation about a “new Yalta”, recalling the 1945 meeting of American, British and Soviet leaders that helped shape the post-war European order.

Story continues below this ad

But the historical analogy has limits. Yalta followed intensive cooperation among the Allies in defeating Nazi Germany. Trump, Putin and Xi are meeting amid expanding rivalry, with little agreement on the rules of the international order. Their immediate objective is to explore common ground rather than negotiate a grand geopolitical bargain.

Unsurprisingly, there is little clarity about the G-3 agenda. Nuclear arms control and cooperation in managing conflicts involving Iran and Ukraine are among the possibilities. Regulating artificial intelligence could be another. For Trump, the meeting reflects his faith in personal diplomacy and his ability to strike grand bargains. But much of the American foreign policy establishment remains sceptical of his approach to Putin and Xi. Any major concession by Trump to Russia and China with produce a vigorous American backlash.

Explained | The last US-Russia nuclear pact ends today. Is this the beginning of a new arms race?

For Putin, Shenzhen offers recognition of Russia’s enduring place at the global high table. Xi’s priorities are different. For Xi, trade, technology and strategic competition with Washington matter more than creating a trilateral institution. Yet Xi has little reason to reject a meeting that pleases Putin while consolidating Beijing’s status as the critical element of a global “triumvirate”.

The relevance for India 

For India, the Quad’s revival offers an opportunity to reboot its troubled relations with Washington. But as part of the hedge against American unpredictability, Delhi will continue to deepen cooperation with Europe, Russia and Japan while seeking to manage the structural tensions with China.

Story continues below this ad
China This Week | Spotlight on Chinese spying in Jensen Huang saga, and a Xi-Trump-Putin meeting

Critics at home and abroad have often derided India’s foreign policy as excessively transactional, especially its attempt to ride several horses, including BRICS and the Quad. But the new reality is that the great powers are doing much the same— balancing and bargaining. That is now baked into the international dynamic today.

Russia is a vociferous critic of America, but it seeks accommodation with Trump. China wants to reduce American influence in Asia but also seeks recognition as Washington’s equal. Neither sees a contradiction in pursuing apparently competing objectives.

For India, strategic flexibility can’t be an end in itself. An open-ended foreign policy, strong international partnerships must go hand in hand with the purposeful modernisation and upgradation of national capabilities. Without domestic unity and strength, India’s multi-alignment runs the risk of remaining trapped in intellectual abstraction rather than becoming a transformative tool towards advancing national interest.

(C. Raja Mohan is a contributing editor on International affairs for the Indian Express. He is professor and director at the Motwani-Jadeja Institute of American Studies, Jindal Global University, Delhi).

title: Who keeps the internet running, and what happens when they can no longer afford to? An expert explains
content_html:
After the PHP2Shell flaws were disclosed, open-source maintainers helped get security fixes to users, including those on older PHP releases. (Magnific)
AI Narration
Listen
00:00

When two critical security flaws in PHP, a programming language used by millions of websites, prompted organisations around the world to take services offline in October, Czech software engineer Ondřej Surý was among the maintainers who helped get the fixes to users.

The flaws, collectively dubbed PHP2Shell, led to precautionary shutdowns on October 21 of services run by Japan’s Finance Ministry, US human-resources platform BambooHR, the Port of Rotterdam in the Netherlands, and the Wikimedia Foundation, which operates Wikipedia.

Surý maintains widely used PHP software packages for Debian and Ubuntu, two Linux-based operating systems. He made patched versions available even for older releases of PHP that no longer receive official security updates.

Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads.

Surý does much of this maintenance alongside his full-time job as Director of DNS Engineering at the Internet Systems Consortium (ISC), which develops software that helps translate website addresses into the numerical addresses computers use to communicate over the internet. He told The Indian Express that ISC had seen a sharp spike in vulnerability reports this year, although relatively few were serious. As AI tools make it easier to identify potential security flaws, assessing and fixing them still requires human expertise.

The experience raises a larger question about the sustainability of open-source software, whose underlying code is freely available for others to use, modify and distribute, and on which much of the internet depends. In an interview with The Indian Express, Surý discusses the PHP2Shell incident, the growing demands of AI-assisted vulnerability discovery, and why he believes businesses that profit from open-source software must help fund its maintenance. Edited excerpts:

Why does PHP matter to the functioning of the internet, and what made the recent PHP2Shell vulnerabilities particularly serious?

PHP is a programming language mainly used to develop websites. Roughly 70% of the web is powered by PHP. The recently discovered vulnerabilities in PHP were in the most serious category, remote code execution (RCE). In short, an attacker can exploit such a vulnerability to execute a program of their own choosing on a remote machine, potentially gaining full access to the server (the computer running the website or service).

When researchers discover a serious security flaw in widely used software, what happens next? Who develops the fix, who ensures it reaches users, and which parts of this process still depend heavily on human work?

Story continues below this ad

When ethical security researchers discover a serious security flaw, they contact the affected project or organisation privately. Any project or organisation that cares about security should have a mechanism through which researchers can report flaws in its software.

Also in Explained | What is PHP2Shell, and why did it force websites around the world offline?

Fixing the vulnerability is usually no different from fixing any other defect in the software, but the process depends on the size of the project. The work could fall to a single person in a small project or a handful of people in a larger one. They might or might not be employed to do this work.

In the case of PHP, there are a handful of volunteers for whom this is a side project, and very few people are employed directly by the PHP Foundation. Most of the important work still depends on people. As for when and how AI is used, it is important to remember that AI is just a tool that might or might not be useful in specific cases.

How did the early disclosure of the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities affect the release of security updates?

Story continues below this ad

That was unfortunate because people who knew the original release schedule had made plans to properly release the software so that users could upgrade. The premature disclosure accelerated the whole process by a day.

Now, this is the bad part about AI: once details of the upcoming vulnerabilities were known, people started using AI to search for possible security flaws. It was no longer safe to stick to the original schedule because AI, as a tool, is quite good at finding security vulnerabilities, especially when guided by a skilled person.

AI tools are increasingly being used to discover vulnerabilities in software. Have you noticed any change in the number or complexity of vulnerability reports you receive, or in the work required to respond to them?

In my day job, I am the Director of DNS Engineering at ISC, responsible for BIND 9, a widely used open-source DNS server. There was a sharp spike this year in the frequency and depth of the vulnerability reports we received.

Story continues below this ad

Fortunately, after the initial surge, things went back to normal. We still receive occasional security reports, but only very few of them are serious enough to be handled as security vulnerabilities.

That is the thing with AI: it needs to be guided by an expert with domain knowledge. Otherwise, you often end up with serious-sounding reports about ordinary software bugs, or issues that are not even bugs.

Could AI also help maintainers identify security vulnerabilities themselves?

Not only that, maintainers can also use frontier AI models to find security vulnerabilities themselves. That said, both offensive (finding and exploiting vulnerabilities) and defensive (finding and fixing vulnerabilities) uses of AI need to be supervised by an expert. Otherwise, you might end up with a pile of mediocre-quality reports or, worse, AI might miss something serious.

You’ve spoken about the difficulty of sustaining open-source maintenance. Why does so much essential software depend on the work of relatively few people, and what would it take to support them adequately?

Story continues below this ad

When I joined university in 1995, free software was still very new, at least to me, and I found a purpose in making the fruits of my work freely available to others. It was a paradigm change, and I believe many people involved in the free-software movement are still driven by those ideals.

Black October | An expert explains how AI is changing cybersecurity

On the other hand, some people have built multibillion-dollar enterprises on top of open-source software and never even thought about supporting the software that allowed them to make money.

I think we need to find a balance. The free-software model is viable because it gives me and other developers freedom. On the other hand, if many people depend on that software for their livelihoods, we need a sustainable model that allows maintainers to continue working on the software they love without becoming exploited and exhausted.

Who should be responsible for funding the maintenance of open-source software?

Story continues below this ad

That question can easily be turned around: if the people maintaining the open-source software your company uses were to simply walk away, how large would your losses be in the event of a serious security vulnerability like the recent one in PHP? This should give people running businesses the answer to who should fund the work.

Not every open-source project has an organisation, whether for-profit or non-profit, behind it, but some do.

For instance, Software in the Public Interest is a non-profit organisation that provides financial and administrative support to projects such as Debian. Smaller projects can raise funds through platforms such as Open Collective, while PHP development receives funding through the PHP Foundation.

My PHP packaging work can be supported through Freexian’s PHP Long Term Support (PHP LTS) project, which provides maintenance and security updates for older PHP releases, or through GitHub Sponsors, which allows individuals and organisations to fund developers directly.

Story continues below this ad

At my day job, the Internet Systems Consortium (ISC) offers paid professional support for open-source projects such as BIND 9 and Kea, among other projects I am closely associated with.

Expert Explains | COP31: What’s at stake at UN climate summit in Antalya
content_html:
A sign for the COP31 UN Climate Summit at the Istanbul Airport in Turkey. Photo: AP/Emrah Gurel/File
AI Narration
Listen
00:00

Written by Indu K Murthy

Starting Monday (November 9), the next chapter of global climate action will unfold in Turkey at the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) until November 20, with about 100,000 participants and heads of state gathering for a World Leaders’ Summit on November 11 and 12.

As the first COP since the United States’ exit from the Paris Agreement earlier this year, COP31 removes the largest historical emitter from finance conversations, sharpening developing countries’ demand that Europe and others fill the gap. Energy security, meanwhile, has taken centre stage. The war on Iran has pushed up oil and gas prices, raising the cost of fuel and food. Supporters of a faster energy transition argue that this shows the risks of fossil-fuel dependence, while importers such as India face more immediate pressure to keep supplies affordable.

Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads.

The questions that matter are how much finance will actually flow to developing countries, how adaptation will be measured and paid for, and whether mounting pressure on coal and emission targets will respect the principle of “common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities” (CBDR-RC).

What is a COP?

A COP is the annual meeting of countries that signed the 1992 UNFCCC. In Antalya, there will be three meetings in focus: COP31, the 21st session of the Conference of Parties serving as the meeting of Parties to the Kyoto Protocol (CMP21), and the 8th session of the Conference of the Parties serving as the meeting of Parties to the 2015 Paris Agreement (CMA8).

Also read | Three steps COP should take for tangible outcomes

The Paris Agreement asks every country to submit a nationally determined contribution (NDC), essentially its own climate plan, every five years, with the shared ambition of holding warming well below 2°C while pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5°C. Because decisions require consensus, a single country can hold up an agreement.

How is COP31 different from previous COPs?

COP venues rotate among the UN’s regional groups, and 2026 was the turn of the “Western European and Others” group to host. Turkey bid with Antalya, and Australia bid with Adelaide, in partnership with Pacific Island nations.

Story continues below this ad

The resulting standoff led to an unusual power-sharing deal last year, making COP31 the first summit where one country hosts the meeting while another runs the negotiations.

Turkey is the formal COP31 president and host, responsible for the venue, logistics, and the “Action Agenda” of voluntary pledges and initiatives, whereas Australia has “exclusive authority” over formal talks, drafting of texts, and steering decisions. This dual leadership model is untested, and questions remain about who would have the final word if there were disagreement in the closing hours. 

What’s on the table?

COP31 is not expected to produce a landmark treaty text. The real fight is over delivery: mobilising finance, measuring progress, and accelerating the energy shift.

In terms of co-chairing consultations, India and Germany must decide on mitigation, as in how to press countries whose 2035 plans fall short of 1.5°C and what “transitioning away from fossil fuels” actually requires. On finance, France and the Philippines will work to build consensus on delivering existing finance commitments. On adaptation, the UK and Sierra Leone must chart a credible path to tripling adaptation finance and make enough headway for the Global Goal on Adaptation (GGA) to be finalised at COP32.

Story continues below this ad
A street vendor walks amid thick haze from wildfires in Indonesia on October 24, 2026. Photo: AP/Yulianus Stefan Lundju/File

Taking on newer ground, Mexico and Poland must work out how the just transition mechanism will function and what money and technical help it will give affected workers and communities. Palau and Canada handle the ocean, where Pacific Island countries want commitments written into formal decisions.

Two more items will set the summit’s tone. Turkey wants countries to pledge to raise electricity’s share of global final energy use from about 23% today to 35% by 2035. Further, developing countries, including India, have pushed to include Article 9.1 of the Paris Agreement, the clause that obligates developed countries to provide finance, in the provisional agenda.

What Belém left behind

The COP30 in Belém, Brazil, closed with a package called the “Global Mutirão” (meaning, collective effort) and Antalya inherits this “to-do” list. It called for adaptation finance to be at least tripled by 2035, five years later than developing countries had wanted and without a clear baseline.

title: Decoding the 2026 US midterms verdict: Why Delhi must rediscover and engage with the many Americas
content_html:
The Democratic Party’s sweeping victory in the American midterm elections presents India with immediate and long-term imperatives in dealing with the United States, its most important and comprehensive partner for the foreseeable future.

The immediate task is to step up engagement with the Trump administration, wrap up the long-pending bilateral trade agreement and advance cooperation in energy, defence and technology.

Advertisement

The latest election is part of the enduring ebb and flow of American politics. The Democratic triumph this week does not guarantee it victory in the 2028 presidential election or continued Congressional domination in the next congressional cycle. Instead of obsessing with mood swings in the American electorate, Delhi must rediscover America’s extraordinary political diversity and rebuild relationships across its rapidly changing political landscape.

It is not just Trump who will fade from the scene in the coming years. Familiar Democratic figures — the Clintons, Obama and Biden — are also yielding to a new generation representing a more diverse America. If India was surprised by the power of the MAGA movement on the right, it must prepare for potential shocks from the rise of progressive forces on the Democratic side.

More immediately, Prime Minister Narendra Modi could have two opportunities to meet Trump — at the East Asia Summit in Manila this month and the G20 summit in Miami in December. These encounters offer Delhi an opportunity to consolidate the partnership after a turbulent period. Trump will remain in office for more than two years and retain considerable authority over foreign policy until his last day in the White House.

Challenges for India’s political class

Advertisement

For the Indian political class, the long-term challenge is threefold.

First, move away from a shallow understanding of America (Republicans are “good”, Democrats are “bad” or vice versa) and an emotional reaction to developments (every remark by an official in DC gets amplified into some kind of a turning point in relations). We need a better appreciation of America’s deep structures, its changing internal dynamics, and their impact on US policies.

Neither the Republican nor the Democratic Party has a settled ideological identity, and divisions within them are often as sharp as those between them. Shifting coalitions across party lines increasingly shape American policies at home and abroad. Grasping the multiple strands of American politics and its changing coalitions is key to successful policy formulation in Delhi.

Also in Explained | US midterms: Key takeaways, impact on the world and India

Second, discard the assumption that Washington needs Delhi more than India needs America. This encouraged needless complacency, which Trump’s second term shattered. A more realistic appreciation of what binds and divides the two countries is essential for stable engagement.

Third, return to the diplomatic playbook that transformed bilateral relations in the 1990s and 2000s. That transformation did not emerge simply from agreements between presidents and prime ministers. It involved patient efforts to seek and win friends across Congress, business, universities, think tanks and the Indian diaspora.

The historic civil nuclear agreement of 2008 was the culmination of a diplomatic playbook that transformed bilateral India-US relations in the 1990s and 2000s. Photo: Wikimedia Commons

The historic civil nuclear agreement of 2008 was the culmination of that effort. It required full backing from the White House, bipartisan support in Congress. It demanded the readiness to engage sceptics and overcome entrenched opposition. Delhi did not assume India’s strategic importance would automatically produce favourable outcomes in Washington. It invested political and diplomatic capital in building a supportive coalition.

That lesson is especially relevant today. America’s federal structure, a powerful legislature, corporations, universities, media and civic organisations create multiple centres of political influence. American politics is not merely a contest between Republicans and Democrats, but a continuing negotiation among competing economic interests, regional identities and ideological traditions.

Transformations within Republicans, Democrats

Trump’s nationalist movement has transformed the Republican Party, challenging traditional commitments to free trade, immigration and international alliances. Yet the party remains divided between economic nationalists, market-oriented libertarians, religious conservatives, and those seeking an end to endless wars.

The Democrats are undergoing an equally consequential transformation. Progressives challenge traditional leaders on inequality, corporate power, defence spending, and foreign policy. Divisions over Israel, the Middle East and military intervention reflect a wider struggle over the party’s international outlook. Anti-war movements on the left share some ground with isolationist sentiments on the right. The midterm results will intensify these debates as both parties prepare for the 2028 presidential contest.

Delhi cannot afford to remain confined to established networks. The task is not merely to cultivate those sympathetic to India, but also to engage critics on trade, immigration, human rights and Russia. India has lost friends among American progressives, and a special effort is needed to reconnect with them. Changing demographics, the growing influence of ethnic minorities and the revival of socialist traditions demand greater Indian attention to the American left.

More in Explained | US midterms: What the setback for Trump means for US-India trade deal

This task cannot be left to the government alone. Indian political parties, civil society and business must deepen engagement with their American counterparts. The BJP and RSS are developing their own independent outreach to America. Rahul Gandhi has frequently travelled to the US, but Congress needs more structured engagement with American society. Indian parties must reach beyond the diaspora to the wider forces shaping American polity.

India will continue to need the American partnership for economic transformation, technological modernisation and regional security. But it cannot rely merely on personal chemistry between leaders or relations between governments of the moment. India needs not just strong ties with the White House, the permanent bureaucracy and Congress, but also a broad and durable constituency of friends across the many Americas.

The author is a contributing editor on international affairs for The Indian Express.

title: Why flight delays make up most travel claims, yet medical bills take 80% of payouts
content_html:
Travel insurance has also become an increasingly popular tool for travellers to safeguard against losses arising from travel disruptions. (AP)
AI Narration
Listen
00:00

When it comes to insurance, claims and settlements happen to be the most important metrics. Data from Asego, a global travel assistance and insurance provider, showed that non-medical claims account for over two-thirds of travel insurance claims in the first nine months of the financial year but just a fifth of total payouts.

Payouts are much better for medical claims, which account for just a third of travel insurance claims but make up 80% of total payouts. The data is based on Asego’s analysis of nearly 11,000 travel insurance claims.

“The analysis brings out two distinct dimensions of travel risk: the frequency of everyday travel disruptions and the potentially substantial financial consequences of medical emergencies,” noted Dev Karvat, Founder and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Asego.

Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads.

So, why is there such disparity between medical and non-medical claim settlements, and what does this data show us?

Why are non-medical claims so frequent?

Non-medical claims consist of issues such as flight cancellations, delays, baggage issues, and stolen belongings, among others. These are very common while travelling, leading to a substantially higher number of claims.

“Flight delays, cancellations, baggage delays, and missed connections are more commonly experienced by travellers. However, the individual payouts are generally smaller and subject to policy limits,” said Ramit Goyal, Chief Distribution Officer at Generali Central Insurance.

Explained | Why everything from flight tickets to pen drives is getting more expensive

A changing global order has also led to higher claims. “Weather disruptions, airline operational issues, geopolitical developments, and complex flight itineraries have increased travellers’ exposure to non-medical risks, contributing to higher claim volumes in these categories,” Goyal added.

Story continues below this ad

The Asego report noted that travel delays and cancellations were the biggest reason for non-medical claims, accounting for 27%. Trip cancellations accounted for 23% of the claims, while delayed baggage contributed to 14%.

“While these incidents may not always involve large individual payouts, their frequency makes them a significant component of travel insurance claims,” said Asego’s Dev Karvat.

Behind the payout gap

While non-medical claims are more frequent, they often cost less to resolve than medical claims.

“The data reflects a fundamental insurance principle — the most frequent claims are not necessarily the most expensive. A relatively small number of high-value medical claims can account for a significant proportion of total payouts,” said Goyal.

Story continues below this ad
Also Read | Why Mumbai airport plans to shift flights to Navi Mumbai by destination, not airline

Healthcare costs are much higher in many international destinations, leading to medical claim payouts ballooning despite a lower number of claims.

Asego’s findings also show the same. According to the company, consolidated data from insurers showed that total cashless and reimbursement payouts between April and November were at $6.7 million, out of which medical claims accounted for $5.3 million and non-medical at $1.3 million.

“The data highlights how a relatively smaller proportion of medical incidents can translate into a significantly higher financial burden,” the report said.

Travel insurance has also become an increasingly popular tool for travellers to safeguard against losses arising from travel disruptions. This popularity is also behind a higher number of non-medical claims, which are more frequent, as per industry executives.

Story continues below this ad

“Travel insurance has now become much more widespread. People are slowly getting how a small amount can save you in case of major mishaps. Thus, higher claims are a part and parcel of this increased attention,” noted an industry executive.

title: Price of war: How India’s oil, gas import bill is soaring amid West Asia crisis
content_html:
In October, the last month for which data is available, the oil import bill jumped 87.5% on-year to $19.5 billion. (Reuters Photo)
AI Narration
Listen
00:00

India’s crude oil import bill surged by nearly 54% on a year-on-year (y-o-y) basis in the first seven months of the current financial year, even as import volumes rose only slightly amid supply tightness and elevated prices owing to the West Asia conflict and the consequent Strait of Hormuz crisis, as per provisional data from the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG).

Elevated prices also led to a jump in liquefied natural gas (LNG) import bill and fuel export value. As a result, net oil and gas imports — arrived at by deducting petroleum product exports from oil, natural gas, and petroleum product imports — were higher by almost 40% from the year-ago levels, underscoring the adverse economic impact of the West Asia crisis on energy import-dependent India.

The country depends on imports to meet over 88% of its crude oil requirement and about half of its consumption of natural gas, which is imported as LNG, or super-chilled gas. Despite depending on imported oil and gas, India is a net exporter of petroleum products due to its massive oil refining capacity, while it also imports some petroleum products like liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads.

Prior to the West Asia war, which broke out in late-February, about 40% of India’s crude oil imports, 60% of its LNG imports, and a whopping 90% of its LPG imports came from the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz.

Although the physical supply tightness — a key worry in the first few months of the war — has now eased to a large extent, energy prices remain elevated and volatile amid sky-high freight and insurance costs owing to war risk premiums. Energy imports are a major component of India’s overall imports, and any meaningful increase has ramifications for the country’s trade balance, current account, inflation, and the rupee’s exchange rate, among others. For instance, India’s wholesale fuel and power inflation was 32.8% in October, 25.9% in September, and 23.2% in August, as per government data.

It also said that every 10% increase in oil price typically widens the country’s current account deficit by 0.4% on the gross domestic product (GDP). Crude oil alone is the country’s largest merchandise import.

Heavy dependence on energy imports has led to a double whammy of supply tightness and price surge. While highly diversified crude sourcing has helped in ensuring adequate oil, petrol, diesel, and jet fuel availability amid the West Asia crisis, some rationing of gas supplies to certain industries and commercial consumers was done in the initial months of the conflict in order to ensure adequate availability for households and a few priority sectors.

title: As India Inc posts record Q2 profit, why top five companies made up a quarter
content_html:
While Indian companies historically get the heat for not reinvesting enough into their businesses and instead hold on to large piles of cash and pay out substantial dividends, data shows that these companies may finally be spending these increased earnings on capital expenditure.
AI Narration
Listen
00:00

India Inc reported record profit during second quarter of the financial year 2027 (Q2FY27), outperforming the Street’s expectations. This comes despite the challenges, which included high raw material costs across most industries due to the ongoing West Asia war.

The 2,600-odd listed companies tracked by the Bank of Baroda reported a record net profit of around Rs 4.5 lakh crore during Q2FY27, up nearly 26% year-on-year (y-o-y). The net sales of these companies grew 21% to around Rs 36 lakh crore, said Aditi Gupta, an economist at the bank.

So, who is making the most money among these companies, and where is the cash going?

Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads.

Who makes money?

Reliance Industries Ltd earned the most profit in the Indian listed space, with its oil business boosting its net profit for the July-September quarter to a record Rs 29,550 crore. State Bank of India’s net profit came in at Rs 23,038 crore. Indian Oil Corporation Ltd reported a profit of Rs 21,630 crore, a sharp reversal from the Rs 2,661 crore loss in the previous quarter.

HDFC Bank Ltd and Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Ltd reported profits of Rs 19,510 crore and Rs 18,538 crore.

Net profit of top five companies.

Together, the top five accounted for a quarter of India Inc’s total profits.

Collectively, the top 10, which also consists of ICICI Bank Ltd, Tata Consultancy Services Ltd, LIC, Bharti Airtel Ltd, and Infosys Ltd, accounted for 38% of India Inc’s profits and nearly 47% of its revenues.

Story continues below this ad

In fact, the top 50 companies, or Nifty 50, make up around 55% of India Inc’s total profits, highlighting that only a handful of companies are driving aggregate profit to record levels. The pace of profit growth was strong all around, with earnings of Nifty 50 companies growing at around 27% y-o-y, while Motilal Oswal’s coverage universe of around 400 companies saw around 32% growth.

Also Read | India Inc’s Budget wish list: Targeted sops, LTCG tax cut, R&D in focus

The growth has been driven by higher volumes across most sectors such as automobiles, banking, and oil, even as margins remain under pressure due to higher costs in the wake of the war in West Asia.

Banks, financial services companies, and oil exploration companies were among the top performers during the quarter, as a high interest rate environment and high crude oil prices proved to be tailwinds. In fact, in the first half of FY27, the profitability of public-sector banks jumped 17% y-o-y to a record Rs 1.1 lakh crore.

Where the cash is going

While Indian companies historically get the heat for not reinvesting enough into their businesses and instead hold on to large piles of cash and pay out substantial dividends, data shows that these companies may finally be spending these increased earnings on capital expenditure. As per Emkay Global, operating cash flow to earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA) ratio of top 500 BSE companies fell to 64% in first half of FY26 from nearly 83% in FY26 and well below the 78-83% seen across FY22-26. This meant companies had lower free cash on their books compared to their operating profit.  “The weakness was concentrated in the cyclicals. Discretionary (25.4% vs 68.0% in FY26), industrials (44.3%), and materials (42.9%). Energy (82.9% vs 106.5%) also moderated,” the report said.

Story continues below this ad
Also Read | No OPD, hospitalisation only Rs 3-5 lakh: Inside India Inc’s staff welfare push

“Some of this is likely due to working-capital build-up in a high-growth phase, and half-year ratios are not strictly comparable with full-year ones; even so, this is the number to track in 2HFY27,” it added.

While this does not mean that cash is being reinvested, as companies also pay out large dividends, data shows that capital expenditure from corporate sector has been picking up in recent times.

While official data for FY27 is not yet out, the Reserve Bank of India’s projections show that private corporate investment may rise about 23% to Rs 3.2 lakh crore in FY27. As per Vinay Jain, Fund Manager and Head of Research at Karma Capital, operating cash flows of top 500 companies on BSE, excluding oil marketing companies, grew 20% in first half of the financial year, compared with just 3% growth in FY26

title: India’s Hindu and Muslim populations will grow by 2070, but only Muslims’ share will rise. Here’s why
content_html:
Shoppers throng Bohri Ali in Pune ahead of Ganesh Chaturthi. A Pew Research Center report projects how India's religious composition, including the shares of Hindus and Muslims, could change by 2070. (Express - Pavan Khengre)
AI Narration
Listen
00:00

By 2070, Hindus will continue to comprise the largest religious group in India but will form a smaller share of the total population — around 75.8%, compared to 79.4% in 2020. The share of Muslims, the second-largest religious group, will rise from 15.2% in 2020 to 19.6% by 2070. The absolute number of both Hindus and Muslims will continue to rise until then.

These findings come from a new Pew Research Center report. The US-based institution regularly analyses and projects trends in demography and religion.

The latest report (“The Future of World Religions: Population Growth Projections, 2020-2070”) was published on Wednesday (November 18) and highlights a major global trend that will be witnessed much sooner. “For centuries, Christianity has been the world’s largest religion. That may soon change. Muslims are expected to outnumber Christians by 2035,” the report says.

Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads.

Here is what it says about India’s religious composition, as well as the larger changes unfolding globally.

What does the report forecast about India’s religious composition?

India religious composition via Pew Research.

Pew considers national surveys and Census data to estimate population changes. It notes that events such as wars, epidemics and natural disasters could affect population changes, but those are outside its ambit. In India’s case, it also noted that the last completed Census was in 2011 and served as the basis of estimation.

With these caveats, here are some of the report’s highlights with respect to India:

* The reason that the share of Muslims will grow as a percentage, even though both Hindu and Muslim populations will increase in absolute numbers, is “mostly because Muslims are younger and have more children than Hindus.”

Story continues below this ad

* While India’s overall fertility rate has fallen rapidly in recent decades, including that of Muslims, it found that “Muslims in India still have more children per woman than Hindus do.” Fertility rate is the average number of children a woman is expected to bear in her lifetime.

As The Indian Express previously reported, according to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s National Family Health Survey (NFHS) – 5 from 2022, Muslims’ fertility rate saw the sharpest decline among all religious communities over the past two decades. It fell to 2.3 in 2019-2021 from 2.6 in 2015-16, but was still the highest among all religious communities at the time. It is expected that the gap among communities will continue to narrow over time.

* “Given this fertility gap and Muslims’ younger age profile, Hindus are projected to decline as a portion of the Indian population, while Muslims are expected to rise,” the report adds.

From the Explained archive | Religions in India, ‘living together separately’

* India has the largest share of Hindus in the world — around 94.5% of the total global Hindu population. “The number of Hindus around the world is projected to increase by 199 million between 2020 and 2070, reaching a total of nearly 1.4 billion,” it says. Non-Hindus, however, will grow at an even faster rate. “As a result, Hindus will shrink slightly as a share of the global population, falling from 15% in 2020 to 14% in 2070.”

Story continues below this ad

* By 2070, India will have the world’s second-largest population of Muslims at 334 million, only behind Pakistan at 461 million. Currently, Indonesia has the largest population of Muslims of any country, while India stands at the third position after Pakistan.

What explains these numbers?

India is the most populous country in the world. Even as fertility rates have fallen significantly in just a few decades, due to improvements in health and infrastructure, women’s education, and shifts in societal attitudes, it continues to have a young population.

As Pew’s report puts it, “The youthfulness of a population is an important factor in future growth.” All else being equal, a younger population means more people in their prime childbearing years, meaning faster population growth than in an ageing society like, say, Japan.

Combined with the age factor, Hindus and Muslims have a 99% “retention rate” — meaning they are extremely unlikely to change their religions over their lifetime — and indicate potential for population growth within those groups

And what are the major global trends?

Story continues below this ad
Global population growth via Pew Research.

ON MUSLIMS OVERTAKING CHRISTIANS: The report says that by 2070, if recent trends continue, there will be more than 3.6 billion Muslims and just under 3 billion Christians worldwide.

It notes that Muslims’ high global fertility is in part driven by sub-Saharan Africa, which is one of the world’s poorest regions. “With a total fertility rate of 5.1 children per woman, Muslims in sub-Saharan Africa far surpass Muslims elsewhere in fertility.” Across religions, too, the region is expected to see higher-than-average population growth in the near future, even as much of the world is witnessing declining fertility rates.

Also in Explained | Power shortage looms: Why states are flocking to spot market as coal stocks dip

ON THE DECLINE AMONG CHRISTIANS: “By 2070, the number of Christians living in sub-Saharan Africa is expected to rise by 896 million, while the number of Christians in the rest of the world is expected to fall by 210 million,” the report says.

The United States currently has the largest Christian population of any country in the world, but the Democratic Republic of the Congo (also a sub-Saharan nation) is projected to assume the top slot by 2070. Declines are also expected in Europe from both demographic factors (i.e., aging populations with low birth rates) and religious switching.

Story continues below this ad

ON PEOPLE WITHOUT RELIGIOUS AFFILIATIONS: “People who have no religious affiliation – sometimes called religious ‘nones’ – are projected to drop substantially as a share of the world population, from 24% in 2020 to 17% in 2070. This is a function of the decline in the overall population of China, which has been contracting for a few years now. The communist nation has strict controls on the practice of religion.

However, 41% of North Americans will be religiously unaffiliated in 2070, up from 30% in 2020. Europe’s non-affiliated people will comprise 33% of the population by then, up from 25% in 2020.

OTHER RELIGIONS: “All other religions combined (including Baha’is, Daoists, Jains, Sikhs, adherents of folk religions and many other groups) are expected to experience a modest increase in number. However, they will slip below 2% of the global population by 2070,” the report adds.

title: NEET-2027: What reforms could be proposed, what more needs to be done
content_html:
The Nandan Nilekani-led high-powered task force must provide a time-bound implementation roadmap that defines institutional responsibilities, resources, technical safeguards, independent oversight, and accountability. Photo: Express
AI Narration
Listen
00:00

Recurring controversies over the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) have exposed persistent vulnerabilities in India’s public examination system. The NEET-2024 examination, which saw paper leaks, exam malpractices, and candidates getting abnormal scores, led to the constitution of the Radhakrishnan Committee — whose 101 recommendations pertained to exam reforms.

Yet, the NEET-2026 examination in May was marked by allegations of paper leaks and cancellations, and the subsequent retest (Re-NEET) in June was followed by widespread student protests. Repeated and incorrect questions as well as answer-key discrepancies have further undermined confidence in competitive examinations.

In July 2026, the government constituted a Nandan Nilekani-led High-Powered Task Force (HPTF) to recommend comprehensive reforms in public examinations, including those conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA). Its initial deadline of October 2026 for submitting its report has been extended to January 2027 after receiving over 50,000 suggestions and extensive stakeholder consultations.

Story continues below. Subscribe to see fewer ads.

With no interim report publicly available, NEET-2027 candidates face considerable uncertainty. With computer-based testing (CBT), a secure question vault, last-minute paper assembly, and digital delivery among the reported proposals, we look at what reforms are likely to be considered, their limitations and challenges, and what needs to be done to restore fairness and institutional accountability beyond NEET-2027.

Why have earlier reforms failed to prevent recurring NEET crises?

Following the NEET-2024 controversy, the Dr Radhakrishnan Committee recommended reforms covering examination security, technology, infrastructure and institutional processes.

But the NEET-2026 crisis raises questions about their implementation and oversight. Vulnerabilities exist across the examination chain — from question setting and review to transportation, storage, examination-centre management, and evaluation. Allegations of insider involvement make these particularly serious.

Story continues below this ad
Also read | Under paper leak shadow, NTA looks for spaces for exam centres; seeks AICTE support next year

New recommendations will have little value unless earlier failures are investigated, institutional responsibility is established, and proposed reforms are rigorously piloted.

Is CBT feasible for NEET?

CBT reduces dependence on physical printing, packaging, transportation, and storage, while enabling computerised administration, controlled access, and automated evaluation. But it introduces digital vulnerabilities, system failures, and cybersecurity risks.

A nationwide examination requires adequate centres, secure systems, reliable power and connectivity, trained personnel, and contingency arrangements. Uneven infrastructure and varying computer familiarity among candidates also raise concerns about accessibility and fairness.

CBT’s feasibility must be established through infrastructure assessment, large-scale pilots, and independent technical audits. Changing the examination format alone cannot guarantee security or fairness.

Story continues below this ad

Can a question vault and last-minute digital delivery secure the question paper?

Security must begin with question creation and validation, not merely paper transportation. Question setting, review, syllabus alignment, translation, and answer verification are all potential points of compromise, particularly with concentrated access.

A proposed question vault would maintain a large pool of independently vetted questions. The final paper could be assembled shortly before the examination, encrypted and digitally transmitted to centers, thereby reducing advance access and dependence on physical transport.

Candidates being screened as they arrive at an examination centre for the RE NEET UG exam in Jaipur on June 21, 2026. Photo: Rohit Jain Paras

The question paper repository, selection software, servers, encryption keys, and transmission networks require restricted access, traceable operations, and independent cybersecurity audits. Ultimately, security depends on the entire chain — from question setters and validators to final selection and delivery.

How can fairness be ensured across multiple CBT sessions?

Story continues below this ad

Multiple NEET sessions require different question papers, yet all candidates must compete on a common merit list. Ensuring equivalent difficulty is therefore a major challenge.

Statistical normalisation, potentially using percentile scores, may help compare performance. But its reliability depends on the comparability of the papers and on statistical assumptions. Even small adjustments can affect ranks and admission prospects.

Also read | NEET moving online: Education Ministry prepares CBT upgrade for future exams

Through rigorous pilots and independent validation, NTA must establish that papers have comparable syllabus coverage, difficulty, and discriminatory power. The methodology and its limitations must be transparent and auditable. Normalisation cannot compensate for fundamentally unequal question papers.

Beyond technical reforms, changes to eligibility, examination schedules, sessions, and format could further reduce vulnerabilities. Such changes require advance notification and phased implementation. In the absence of timely official announcements, major structural changes to NEET-2027 should be ruled out.

Can a two-stage NEET examination address normalisation concerns?

Story continues below this ad

A two-stage examination, on the lines of IIT-JEE (Mains and Advanced), is one possible alternative. All eligible candidates would appear in a screening examination (Mains), followed by a final examination for shortlisted candidates (Advanced) based on predefined cut-offs or a specified number of qualifiers. A single-session final examination does not need normalisation.

This model raises questions about shortlisting, eligibility, syllabus, question paper format and difficulty, scoring, and cut-offs. It would increase examination overheads but improve fairness in rankings for top scorers.

Should Class XII marks carry weightage in NEET? Can NEET be conducted twice a year?

On Tuesday (November 17), The Indian Express reported that providing weightage to Class 12 board exam scores in NEET-UG has emerged as a key proposal from several states during “consultative meetings” held so far with the Nilekani-led task force. Another proposal discussed was offering more than one attempt in a year.

Also read | States to Nandan Nilekani task force: Give weightage to Class 12 board exam scores in NEET UG

Weightage to Class XII marks could recognise sustained academic performance, but variations in board examinations and marking standards make equitable weightage difficult. Conducting NEET twice a year could offer candidates another opportunity to improve their scores, but would increase logistical costs and raise concerns about normalisation and admission timelines.

Story continues below this ad

A two-stage NEET, along the lines of IIT-JEE, could address both concerns: Class XII marks could be used in determining eligibility for the second-stage single-session examination.

Could the HPTF recommend changes to eligibility, attempts, or age limits?

With over two million candidates competing for limited medical seats, NEET’s unlimited attempts and the absence of an upper age limit raise questions about the examination’s capacity and the size of the candidate pool. Candidates can appear repeatedly, irrespective of age, even beyond 60.

Age limits and attempt restrictions, common in most competitive examinations, could help narrow the candidate pool.

Story continues below this ad

Can GenAI improve question generation and the quality of examinations?

Conventional software can select pre-vetted questions from a secure vault without GenAI. GenAI could assist in question generation, syllabus mapping, translation, preparing answer options, and calibrating difficulty, creating a larger, more diverse question pool.

Also read | CISF, AI monitoring, security experts: How NTA is changing after NEET leak

AI-generated questions, however, may contain factual errors, ambiguities, incorrect answer keys, syllabus errors, or translation defects. Expert validation is essential; AI may assist question development.

What should the HPTF deliver to restore confidence in public examinations?

Story continues below this ad

The Nilekani-led HPTF must provide a time-bound implementation roadmap that defines institutional responsibilities, resources, technical safeguards, independent oversight, and accountability. Major reforms must undergo large-scale pilots before nationwide implementation.

NTA also needs permanent expertise in examination management, cybersecurity, psychometrics, digital forensics, and vigilance. The HPTF’s success must ultimately be measured by whether examinations become secure, transparent, reliable, and fair. India needs not merely new examination technology but also trustworthy examination standard operating procedures and institutions.

The author is a former computer science professor at IIT Kharagpur, IIT Kanpur, BITS Pilani and JNU, and a former scientist at the Defence Research and Development Organisation and the Department of Science & Technology.
